document.title: Afghanistan: [Excised] Briefs Ambassador on his Activities. Pleads for Greater Activism by U.N. (Islama 007343)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Confidential] Previously released in The Taliban File Part III. An excised source describes efforts toward multi-ethnic negotiations. Ambassador Simons says Pakistan has a 'privileged association' with the Taliban but not control, is a party rather than a mediator, and cites 'trucks and busses full of adolescent mujahid' crossing the frontier.

events.description: Previous meeting of the Pakistani interlocutor with US officials (reftel A).
Trip to Tehran Aug 4-5 for talks with Borujerdi.
Dubai meeting with Qanuni, who agreed to drop the Kabul demilitarization pre-condition.
Kandahar meeting with Mullah Hassan and Mullah Jalil; proposal to split political commission into ceasefire/prisoner and multi-ethnic government tracks.
Meeting with Masood in Farkhar, who promised help obtaining release of the four peace emissaries.
Major problem within Pakistani government over wheat price (10 vs 6.5 rupees/kg) for supplies to Afghans.
US Embassy Islamabad cable reports on the briefing and requests US support for OIC vacant-seat policy.
Pakistani official received by Masood in Farkhar; Masood promised to help obtain release of four prisoners, but nothing materialized.
Pakistani official traveled to Tehran, met Borujerdi and discussed shared objectives in Afghanistan.
Meeting in Frankfurt of Afghan parties (including Arsala and others), read out by Qanuni.
Qanuni briefed the Pakistani official on the Frankfurt meeting and pleaded for GOP help establishing a political commission; agreed to drop Kabul demilitarization precondition.
In Kandahar the Pakistani official met Mullah Hassan and another mullah and proposed splitting a political commission into ceasefire/prisoner exchange and future government tracks.
Pakistani ministers told the official in late June to act or face a deadline, prompting his active mediation.
Dispute within Pakistani government over wheat price (10 vs 6.5 rupees/kg) for Afghan sales raised at cabinet by Gohar Ayub Khan.
Ambassador Simons briefed by Pakistani official on his Afghan activities; discussion of UN role, conference proposal and Pakistan aid to Taliban (cable date).
ISI figure: total Pakistani aid to Taliban through end of 1996 was 20 million rupees.
Excised Pakistani official's previous meeting with the US Embassy (REFTEL A); the cable updates events since then.
Trip to Tehran on August 4-5 for talks with Borujerdi; briefly met an Iranian official and awaited Qanuni's arrival from Frankfurt.
Meeting with Qanuni in Dubai; Qanuni agreed to drop demilitarization of Kabul as a pre-condition but demurred on prisoners.
Meeting in Kandahar with Mullah Hassan and Mullah Jalil; proposal to split the political commission into a ceasefire/prisoner-exchange track and a multi-ethnic government track.

Shuttle diplomacy between Mazar-i-Sharif and Kandahar with a side trip to Farkhar, where Masood welcomed the Pakistani party and promised to help obtain release of the prisoners (undated, apparently July).

In early July the Taliban's stated pre-condition was only the release of four 'peace emissaries' (including Mullah Ghaus and Mullah Ehsan); a week later it agreed to talk to Malik with no pre-conditions, a promise never honored.
Qanuni met in Frankfurt with a party whose identity is excised; he later briefed the Pakistani official in Tehran (the read-out was of the Frankfurt meeting).
The Taliban, Jumbesh, Jamiat and Hezb-i-Wahdat agreed in principle to set up a political commission on the future government of Afghanistan, but pre-conditions blocked its establishment.
Brahimi's delayed arrival and refusal to stay in Kandahar prevented a planned meeting with Mullah Omar.
The GOP asked the US to support the OIC 'vacant seat policy' on Afghanistan at the UN and urged UNSMA to be more active.
The US Embassy Islamabad cable reports the briefing and asks for action.

sources_cited: ISI figure on aid to the Taliban
key_claims: Pakistan says it has a 'privileged association' with the Taliban but not control over them.
The US ambassador argues Pakistani aid to the Taliban (wheat, fuel, trucks and buses of volunteers with short training) far exceeds the 20 million rupee ISI figure.
The US ambassador says Pakistan is a party to the conflict rather than just a mediator, so the UN mediating role is essential.
The Taliban held Mullah Ghaus, Mullah Ehsan and two other 'peace emissaries' as prisoners in Gen. Malik's custody and made their release a key pre-condition.
The Pakistani government believes the Northern Alliance would collapse if the Taliban ceased military activity.
Pakistan believes the Taliban will eventually win and then yield to technocrats such as Arsala, a view the US ambassador disputes.
Iran, Uzbekistan and Russia are described as having privileged associations with northern factions analogous to Pakistan's with the Taliban.
